channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Watchdog clashes with Palantir over threat to health data
item.description: The National Data Guardian has warned that public concern about the federated data platform may undermine the quality of health data – prompting Palantir to accuse her of being “captured by campaign groups”.

item.title: Government accused of ‘suppressing’ concerning maternity report
item.description: Leading campaigners have accused ministers of “suppressing” a report that is understood to set out significant concerns raised by families harmed by their experiences of maternity care investigations.

item.title: Long-awaited children’s cancer move delayed again
item.description: The transfer of a children’s cancer service, ordered after years of safety concerns, has been delayed again and will not happen before 2028.

item.title: NHSE-DHSC salary gap revealed
item.description: NHS England pay packages are, on average, more than 15 per cent, or £9,500, higher than in the Department of Health and Social Care, an analysis by HSJ has found.

item.title: New chair for ICB facing £136m deficit
item.description: An experienced integrated care board leader has been drafted in to chair a board overseeing one of the country’s most troubled systems.

item.title: Medics accused of ‘misappropriating’ data to set up firm
item.description: A doctor misappropriated confidential documents from a major NHS diagnostics supplier and shared them with his associates to set up a rival private business, it is alleged.

item.title: The 75 most influential Black, Asian and minority ethnic people in health: Full list
Union calls new trust CEO’s claim ‘simply untrue’
item.description: A trade union has accused a troubled trust’s new interim chief executive of making a “simply untrue” claim to staff that he had met its representatives to resolve a strike by theatre workers.

item.title: Trust under manslaughter investigation over four deaths
item.description: An ongoing potential corporate manslaughter investigation is looking into the deaths of four patients on a stroke ward, a court has heard.

item.title: Nursing regulator makes U-turn over snooping cases
item.description: Nurses are now facing regulatory action for improperly viewing Southport attack victim files after a U-turn by their regulator – which was made only after the breaches became public, HSJ can reveal.

item.title: ICBs in the dark about quality of private care, warns government review
item.description: A government-commissioned review has expressed “strong concerns” over the consistency and quality of ADHD and autism assessments carried out by private providers.

item.title: Trust CEOs to join NHSE top team
item.description: Northumbria Healthcare Foundation Trust CEO Birju Bartoli is to join NHSE as lead for urgent and emergency care.

item.title: Hospital performance on the slide across the board
item.description: NHS secondary care performance deteriorated in almost every area during the past two months.

item.title: NHSE: Boards must ‘account for progress’ on staff vaccination
item.description: Trust boards must be prepared to “account for progress” on their staff flu vaccination rates, NHS England has warned, after only one in 10 providers hit the national ambition last winter.

item.title: UPDATED: Strikes suspended while union considers offer
item.description: Lorry drivers based at all seven NHS Supply Chain warehouses have suspended their strike while a pay offer is considered.

item.title: Hospitals seek ‘pause’ on ambulance handover rule
item.description: An ambulance trust is “not assured” the 45-minute limit on hospital handovers can be consistently delivered this winter, after repeated requests from hospitals to “pause” it.

item.title: At least 20% of baby deaths ‘potentially avoidable’
item.description: At least a fifth of baby deaths last year may have been preventable, with this estimate considered “a minimum”, an analysis of thousands of care reviews has concluded.

item.title: NHS bosses admit defeat on 18-week pledge
item.description: NHS chiefs have told ministers that their top health manifesto pledge - to restore the 18-week elective target by 2029 - is “not going to happen”, as a new analysis confirms the service is significantly off track.

item.title: More execs face losing pay rise under ‘punitive’ rules
item.description: Executives at a “large number” of trusts and integrated care boards could lose their annual pay rise under new oversight rules, the NHS Alliance has warned.

item.title: ICB mergers suspended due to ‘devolution discussions’
item.description: Twenty clustered integrated care boards that had expected to merge next year must wait until at least 2028 while government considers the implications of the prime minister’s devolution agenda, they have been told.
